title: There is a person behind every check-in.

slides.headline: Someone is expecting your check-in.
slides.body: A field worker and their response team need a clear communications plan.

slides.headline: Sent. Received. Acknowledged?
slides.body: Define what the worker and response team see at every message state.

slides.headline: Who takes the next step?
slides.body: Set retry, alternate-path and human escalation rules for each event.

slides.headline: And when no message gets through?
slides.body: Make communication limits visible and define the worker's procedure for that state.

slides.headline: Build the whole safety plan.
slides.body: Review the workflow with technical and safety owners; connectivity is not a safety guarantee.

technicalNotes.headline: Connectivity is one safety layer
technicalNotes.body: Treat it as part of a governed process—not a guarantee.

technicalNotes.headline: Define acknowledgement
technicalNotes.body: Know how the device, worker and response team see message state.

technicalNotes.headline: Define escalation
technicalNotes.body: Set retry, alternate path and human escalation behaviour for each event class.

technicalNotes.headline: Define the unavailable state
technicalNotes.body: The product and procedure must make communication limits visible.

technicalNotes.headline: Assess the dependency
technicalNotes.body: Review the complete safety workflow with technical and risk owners.
